name: Executive order of February 7, 1879 setting apart a reservation for the Muache, Capote and Weeminuche Ute
nations: Southern Ute Indian Tribe (Muache and Capote bands)
promises: In compliance with the agreement of November 9, 1878, the President set apart a reservation for the Muache, Capote and Weeminuche bands bounded by the 37th parallel, 107 degrees west longitude and the "National Divide" of the San Juan Mountains.
today: Royce records that this reservation was restored to the public domain by executive order of August 4, 1882. No court, Indian Claims Commission or congressional finding about this reservation or its restoration was found; the Indian Claims Commission's Southern Ute case (Docket 328) was dismissed in 1971 after United States v. Southern Ute Tribe, 402 U.S. 159.

openQuestions: The 1882 restoration of this reservation would be an executive reduction; no finding about it was located, so it is not counted as a breach.
The agreement this order carried out was never ratified (see cession-1878-11-09-uta-muncho-capote-wiminuehi-bands).
The tribes' own accounts were not found in this pass.
